seeds.context: Swoveralls sells a comfort-first overall/jumpsuit-style loungewear line (Swoveralls, Swovie Shorts, Comfyalls, Corduroy and Grid Fleece versions) priced $89-$159, with 41 core products, many of them limited edition or new. It also offers Kids Swoveralls ($43.99-$49) and a merch range of Sidekick Tees, beanies and hats ($25-$36) with playful graphics and slogans like 'Free Your Waistband' and 'Good at Naps'. Materials seen are cotton, spandex and polyester, and pocket counts of 5, 6 and 7 are called out in the catalogue.
questions: Which ad hooks, formats and angles are performing best right now across the best consumer brands in any industry (on Meta, TikTok and Instagram), and how could Swoveralls adapt them to its own product and playful, comfort-first voice?

How do leading comfort-focused apparel brands such as oversized loungewear and wearable-blanket companies position their products, run limited-edition drops and market to both adults and kids, and which creative angles could Swoveralls use for its $89-$159 overall range and Kids line?
